chapter: Blues, cabarets and the Golden Room
title: Blind Charlie's blues playing
summary: Barnes says Charlie worked in tonks and cabarets with a short man and played more melody; Barnes struggles to describe his blues.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: I want to know more about Blonde Charlie. That's a guy I don't know much about. Who did he work with?
He always worked with a short man. And he worked more in the thunk and cabaret. He's a pretty good clarinets player. He played blues? Oh yeah.
Could you describe the kind of blues he played?
Oh honey. What's the matter? Oh man, I couldn't have any things left.

I couldn't have any. All they say, I'll tell you about the blues is, uh, set the right hand seat ten thousand miles away. Got to the poor portion. One of the blues didn't have another blues. I'm wondering if Matt Bach and Homer could. Well now let's see. Now I'm going, I'm going. Ain't coming back no more.
Did Charlie have anything he featured, like long notes, or did he play a lot of notes? How did he get that feeling in his playing?
More of a melody. He gave up with something extra, you know. That was all.
You can't hum like he played?
No. In fact I can't hum at all.
Yeah you can. You hum like Buddy Bowling for me one day.
I wasn't told. Well did he sound anything like you when you played the blues?
